title: The Harbor of the Lower Danube
premise: In 1854, on the fever-stricken banks of the lower Danube, Ines Amberdale works as a battlefield nurse by day and keeps a secret ledger of the dead and disappeared whom officers refuse to record. When a mute child is abandoned at the harbor workshop of a drowned shipwright, carrying instructions to forget his face, Ines discovers the boy is the sole heir to a shipping fortune — and that powerful men are erasing every trace of him to claim it. As cholera, war, and hired killers close in, Ines must use his ledger of the forgotten to prove the boy's identity before the estate is signed away. The novel ends with Ines testifying at a riverfront inquiry, trading his own anonymity for justice: the child restored, the ledger entered into official record, and Ines leaving the harbor with nothing but his name, which at last means something.
about_author: Ansel Ravensworth is the pen name of a former merchant-marine clerk who spent years cataloguing port records along the Danube's eastern reaches. He writes historical fiction about the people official histories leave off their pages.

chapters.title: The Ledger Under the Cot
chapters.summary: Ines Amberdale's POV. At a makeshift hospital above the Galati harbor, Ines tends wounded soldiers while secretly recording names the officers' reports omit. We learn his rule: keep busy hands, keep a low profile. Emotional beat: quiet defiance born of grief for a brother erased from an earlier war's rolls.

chapters.title: A Child at the Workshop Door
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Summoned to the flooded shipwright's workshop to inventory a dead man's tools, Ines finds a mute boy asleep among the sawdust with a note pinned to his coat: forget the face. Emotional beat: unease hardening into resolve; Ines cannot forget faces — it is his whole trade.

chapters.title: The Drowned Shipwright
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, with flashback. Ines pieces together the last days of Anton Vess, the shipwright who drowned under questionable circumstances, and realizes the boy arrived after the death, not before. Emotional beat: suspicion; the harbor's kindness has a current beneath it.

chapters.title: Names Omitted
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Cross-referencing his ledger against harbor manifests, Ines finds Vess's crew listed as lost at sea — though three men were seen alive last week. Emotional beat: cold clarity that someone is editing reality, and he alone keeps the original text.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A polite magistrate, Corvin Hale, visits the workshop asking after 'strays,' offering coin for any child found. Ines lies smoothly for the first time in his careful life. Emotional beat: fear mixed with exhilaration; his invisibility becomes a weapon.

chapters.title: What the Boy Won't Say
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The boy, whom Ines calls Miri, communicates through drawings: a house, a seal ring, a woman's hand pushing him toward the door. Emotional beat: tenderness breaking through Ines's self-protective distance; he begins to love what he must protect.

chapters.title: The Amberdale Rule
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, deep backstory chapter. Flashback to Ines's brother, expunged from regimental records after a massacre the army denied, and how their mother died waiting for a name on paper. Emotional beat: the origin of the ledger revealed as an act of mourning turned method.

chapters.title: Three Men Alive
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines tracks one of Vess's 'drowned' crewmen to a tavern and hears fragments: a will, a seal, a payment from the Meridian Shipping House. The man vanishes before dawn. Emotional beat: dread accelerating; witnesses are being subtracted one by one.

chapters.title: Cholera Season
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Fever sweeps the harbor quarter; the hospital overflows and Ines works thirty hours straight, hiding Miri among the convalescent children where no searcher looks. Emotional beat: exhaustion transfigured into purpose — the sickroom becomes a sanctuary.

chapters.title: Hale's Second Visit
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Magistrate Hale returns with soldiers, searching the workshop legally now, and nearly discovers Miri behind a false bulkhead Vess built. Emotional beat: terror and its aftermath; Ines understands the law itself is the instrument against them.

chapters.title: The Widow Vess
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Elena Vess, presumed dead, alive in Bucharest, narrating how she smuggled her son downriver and why she chose Ines — she had read his name in a nurse's letter years ago. Emotional beat: revelation that Ines was chosen, not chanced upon.

chapters.title: The Meridian House
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Posing as a records clerk, Ines enters the shipping house and finds the forged succession papers already drawn, awaiting only proof of the heir's death. Emotional beat: outrage sharpened into strategy; he copies everything into his ledger.

chapters.title: A Name in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines discovers his own brother's name appears in Meridian's old correspondence — the firm helped bury the massacre evidence years ago. Emotional beat: personal wound fused to public cause; this is no longer charity but reckoning.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Hospital
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A fellow nurse, desperate for cholera medicine for her own family, sells word of Miri's hiding place. Soldiers come at night; Ines escapes with the boy through the flooded timber yards. Emotional beat: heartbreak at human weakness, and forgiveness offered anyway.

chapters.title: Downriver
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines and Miri flee by barge toward Bucharest, pursued along the banks, the ledger wrapped in oilcloth against his chest. Emotional beat: fugitive intimacy; the boy speaks his first word — Ines's name.

chapters.title: Elena's Testimony
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. Reunited mother and son, but Elena is dying of the fever she caught in hiding. She gives Ines her sworn statement and the true seal ring, making him guardian of the truth rather than the child. Emotional beat: grief and trust entwined; inheritance redefined as testimony.

chapters.title: The Inquiry Announced
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. News arrives that an imperial commission will sit at the harbor to settle the Vess estate in six days — unless the heir is produced or proven dead. Hale moves openly now, burning the workshop. Emotional beat: the clock made visible; ash on the water.

chapters.title: Witnesses Raised from the Dead
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Using his ledger, Ines finds the two surviving 'drowned' crewmen hiding in the quarantine sheds and persuades them to testify by promising what no one else could: their real names, spoken aloud, entered into record. Emotional beat: the ledger's purpose fulfilled — restoring the erased.

chapters.title: The Harbor of the Lower Danube
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Before the commission, Ines reads the ledger aloud — the omitted dead, the forged manifests, the living witnesses — then presents Miri and the seal. Hale produces a counter-witness; the room turns. Emotional beat: climax; one voice against an institution, holding.

chapters.title: What Hale Knew
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The counter-witness falters when Miri, speaking now, identifies Hale's own clerk from the night of the abduction. Hale is arrested; the estate stays with the child. Emotional beat: catharsis without triumph — justice done, costs tallied.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Elena dies at peace; the estate's guardians offer Ines reward and position, and he declines both, asking instead that the ledger be copied into the imperial archive under every name it holds, including his brother's. Emotional beat: mourning completed; anonymity surrendered willingly.

chapters.title: Busy Hands
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, epilogue. A year later, Ines nurses in a new port town, unrecognized, his ledger's copy bound in the archive. A woman leaves a frightened child at his door with a note: they said you remember faces. He does. Emotional beat: quiet, cyclical hope — the work continues.
